messages:
Miguel: Heads-up — after the 07:12 rollout we see collector hosts spiking. p99 CPU jumps from ~55% to ~88% for the otel-collector process. Suspect span volume change.
benchbot: automated-metrics snapshot: collector-group-a | cpu_p99=88.2 | spans/s=118k | elk-indexed=~59k | memory_rss=3.1G :bar_chart: 
Tara: rough timeline? which service started producing the extra spans?
Miguel: New debug tracing in routing-service. It started at 07:10. Spans/s baseline ~18k -> 118k (6.5x). Most are short debug spans with full attribute sets.
Sam: if attrs exploded we'll pay per-span CPU. Can you grab collector logs and config? Also which exporter (otlp/grpc vs kafka) are we using?
Miguel: Using OTLP/gRPC to our internal exporter cluster. Collector config attached below (snip).
Miguel: ```processors:
  batch:
    timeout: 10s
    send_batch_size: 512
    send_batch_max_size: 1024
exporters:
  otlp:
    endpoint: otlp-ef-01.redwood.internal:4317
    compression: none
service:
  pipelines:
    traces:
      receivers: [otlp]
      processors: [batch]
      exporters: [otlp]
```
Olga: two quick levers: 1) bump send_batch_size and batch timeout, 2) enable gzip compression on the exporter (trades CPU on exporter side but saves network & receiver CPU spikes). Also consider dropping debug-level spans with a filter processor.
Nate: +1 on filter processor. We can use attributes to route debug spans into a low-retention pipeline. E.g. `attributes` processor to set `trace.pipeline=debug` then pipeline with small retention and cheaper export path.
Sam: also consider tail-based sampling for long-lived traces, but for spammy short spans a head-based sampling/filter is cheaper. Quick test: increasing batch `send_batch_size` from 512 -> 2048 reduced per-span overhead in previous runs.
Miguel: did quick A/B on a canary collector: send_batch_size=2048, timeout=20s, compression=gzip -> CPU p95 down to ~62% but p99 still ~78%. Latency for trace ingest slightly higher (median +6ms).
Tara: p99 still high — maybe the exporter cluster backpressure is causing retries and CPU loops. Any queue-full logs?
Miguel: saw exporter retry logs and `retry_queue_size` creep. Sample from logs: 
```
2026-03-18T07:24:11Z otel-collector exporter/otlp send failed: rpc error: code = ResourceExhausted desc = server overloaded; requeue 120
2026-03-18T07:24:12Z otel-collector processor/batch send_batch failed: retrying after backoff
```
Olga: that confirms backpressure. Two-pronged: reduce incoming volume (filter/sampling) AND scale exporter consumers or use a lossy path for debug spans. Also tune `retry_on_failure` and `max_retries` so collector threads don't spin.
Nate: we should also look at attribute cardinality. Routing-service sets `http.user_email` and many custom tags; strip high-cardinality attrs at the collector before batching. That reduces memory churn.
Sam: suggestion checklist: 
- add `attributes` processor to drop `user_email`, `session_id` for debug spans
- route debug spans to `debug_pipeline` with its own exporter to S3/kafka with 7d retention
- increase batch sizes and enable gzip on otlp
- bump collector replicas and give exporters more throughput (scale exporter pool)
- add `retry_on_failure: false` for non-critical pipelines (or reduce max_retries)

Tara: who can make the attributes+pipeline change quickly so we can mitigate this evening? We want a low-risk change.
Miguel: I can patch collector config with `attributes` drop and a `debug` pipeline, then deploy to canary group A by 08:00.
infra-bot: deploy request: collector-config/177978-healing-patch -> canary-group-a queued (by Miguel) :gear: 
Miguel: patch ready, creating PR now. Link: https://github.com/redwood/telemetry/pull/1829 
Sam: after we stabilize, let's schedule a short postmortem: root cause is unguarded debug tracing + no attr-drop rule + exporter capacity mismatch. Also add a dashboard widget for spans/s per service and pipeline queue length.
Tara: agree. Action items: Miguel -> deploy canary patch; Nate -> prepare quick exporter scale (k8s HPA) and compression toggle; Sam -> update runbook for backpressure signs; Olga -> make retention/route proposal for debug spans. We'll regroup 09:15. :white_check_mark: 
Miguel: thanks — will update thread after canary results.
benchbot: canary metrics (10m after patch): collector-group-a | cpu_p99=64.7 | spans/s=31k | exporter_retries=3 -> significantly lower than before. :sparkles:
Miguel: nice, looks like filters + batching helped. Will keep monitoring and follow up with PR for production rollout.
